definitions.definition: I={i in Z : 0 <= i <= lambda}. Nonnegative indices and factorial arguments are identified with their natural-number values.
For i in I, e_i=(1/i!) y^i v, where y^0 is the identity and powers mean composition.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0 <= lambda < p.
V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda, of complex dimension lambda+1. The given Chevalley operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y, and xy-yx=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.
For natural numbers a and t with t<=a, binom(a,t) t! (a-t)!=a!, where binom(a,t) is the natural binomial coefficient.
source_conditions: a and t are natural numbers.

output.statement: n=lambda+1>0, I has n elements, dim_C V=n, and (e_i)_{i in I} is a complex basis of V, with e_0=v. For every integer t>=0, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. All y^t v vanish for t>lambda. The matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. For every i in I and r>=0, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r<=i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power coefficients are integers.

locals.declaration: Use t as the induction index for the two formulas about y^t v.

argument.text: From H001, n=lambda+1 is positive and the integer interval I has n members. H002 gives dim_C V=n. We prove for every t>=0 that h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v and, for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. The h formula at t=0 is H003. Using hy=yh-2y from H002, the h formula at t+1 follows by applying y to its value at t and subtracting 2y^{t+1}v. For x, the first case is xyv=(yx+h)v=lambda v by H002 and H003. In the step t>=1 assume the two formulas at t (L1). The identity xy=yx+h gives x y^{t+1}v=y(xy^t v)+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+lambda-2t]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. The analogous h step has just been verified. Discharge L1 into the induction step and apply natural induction. This proves both formulas for all their stated indices.

produces.statement: n>0, card(I)=n, dim_C V=n; for all nonnegative integers ell, h y^ell v=(lambda-2ell)y^ell v, and for ell>=1, x y^ell v=ell(lambda-ell+1)y^{ell-1}v.

argument.text: For every i in I, repeated application of F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v; at i=0 the product is 1. Each factor for positive i is a positive integer, hence nonzero in C, and H003 gives v!=0. Thus e_i!=0. By F001 their h-eigenvalues lambda-2i are distinct in C. For any relation sum_{i in I} a_i e_i=0, and any j in I, apply product_{k in I,k!=j}(h-(lambda-2k)Id). The result is a_j product_{k!=j}(2k-2j)e_j=0; all factors and e_j are nonzero. Hence every a_j=0. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n, so they are a basis. F001 says that y^{lambda+1}v, if nonzero, would have eigenvalue -lambda-2. Expanding it in this basis and comparing coefficients in the h-eigenvector equation forces every coefficient to vanish, because -lambda-2 differs from every lambda-2i with i in I. Therefore y^{lambda+1}v=0 and all higher powers vanish. Dividing F001 by i! and using the definition of e now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} within the interval, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. Also e_0=v.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V, e_0=v, y^ell v=0 for all ell>lambda; xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I.

argument.text: Iterating the matrices in F002, x^r e_i/r! has coefficient [(lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)]/r! at e_{i-r} when r<=i, and y^r e_i/r! has coefficient [(i+1)...(i+r)]/r! at e_{i+r} when i+r<=lambda. Empty products are one. M006, with (a,t)=(lambda-i+r,r) and (i+r,r) respectively, identifies these coefficients with binom(lambda-i+r,r) and binom(i+r,r): cancel the nonzero factorial (a-r)! in a!=binom(a,r)r!(a-r)!. The coefficients are natural integers. If r>i, iterating x reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>lambda, iterating y reaches ye_lambda=0. This proves the full divided-power formulas, together with F001 and F002, hence the entire asserted characteristic-zero statement.

applications.bindings: For every i in I and 0<=r<=i set a=lambda-i+r and t=r for X; for 0<=r and i+r<=lambda set a=i+r and t=r for Y.
hypothesis_checks: All indices are nonnegative integers because i<=lambda, r>=0 and i>=0.
For X, a-r=lambda-i>=0; for Y, a-r=i>=0. Thus t<=a in both instances.
